root_cause.text: The `q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare()` function lacks a guard to prevent multiple graph opens when the prepare callback is invoked repeatedly, causing the same graph resource to be opened multiple times without closing the previous instance, leading to resource leaks.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `&& dai_data->graph[dai->id] == NULL` to the playback stream condition before calling `q6apm_graph_open()`. This ensures the graph is only opened if it hasn't already been opened (i.e., when the graph pointer is NULL). Without this check, repeated calls to prepare would repeatedly open new graph instances, leaking the previously opened graph resources since they are never closed before being overwritten.

Author: Srinivas Kandagatla <srini@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Oct 26 12:16:53 2021 +0100

    ASoC: qdsp6: audioreach: add q6apm lpass dai support
    
    Add support to Audio port dais on LPASS Audio IP using
    existing common q6dsp-lpass-ports.
    
    Signed-off-by: Srinivas Kandagatla <srinivas.kandagatla@linaro.org>
    Reviewed-by: Pierre-Louis Bossart <pierre-louis.bossart@linux.intel.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211026111655.
bic_trace_step.reason: The `q6apm_lpass_dai_prepare()` function (lines 120-159) lacks a guard to prevent multiple graph opens. The vulnerability exists because: (1) For PLAYBACK streams, the function calls `q6apm_graph_open()` at lines 133-139 and assigns the result to `dai_data->graph[graph_id]` without checking if a graph already exists at that index. (2) If `prepare()` is called multiple times (which can happen in audio streaming scenarios), it will open a new graph and overwrite the previous pointer without closing it, causing a resource leak. (3) The `q6apm_lpass_dai_startup()` function (lines 161-174) similarly opens graphs for CAPTURE streams without guards. (4) There is no check like `if (dai_data->graph[graph_id] != NULL)` before calling `q6apm_graph_open()` to prevent re-opening an already-open graph. The shutdown function properly closes the graph, but the prepare function can be called multiple times before shutdown, leading to leaked resources.
